title: DNA Quantification Using PicoGreen in Microplates
author: Jenn Coughlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbjdiki6

steps.title: Equilibrate PicoGreen reagent
steps.instruction: Allow the Quant‑iT PicoGreen reagent to warm to room temperature before opening the vial; wrap the frozen vial in aluminum foil, place it in a desk drawer, and allow about one hour for complete thawing because the reagent is light‑sensitive.

steps.title: Prepare 1× TE buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the supplied 20× TE stock with sterile de‑ionized water to obtain 1× TE buffer (exact dilution factor as indicated by the manufacturer).

steps.title: Make PicoGreen working solution
steps.instruction: In a plastic Falcon tube (wrapped in aluminum foil, do not use glass), dilute the thawed PicoGreen reagent 1:200 (PicoGreen : final volume) with 1× TE to create the working solution. Prepare enough for all samples plus extra for pipetting errors; you will need 48 µL of this solution per sample.

steps.title: Create Lambda DNA standard curve
steps.instruction: Using the supplied Lambda DNA stock (100 ng/µL or 100 µg/mL) and 1× TE, prepare eight standard tubes as follows (adjust volumes proportionally if more than two plates are run):

substeps.instruction: Tube 1: 10 µL TE + 10 µL Lambda DNA → 50.0 ng/µL, final volume 10 µL
Tube 2: 10 µL TE + 10 µL from Tube 1 → 125.0 ng/µL, final volume 10 µL
Tube 3: 10 µL TE + 10 µL from Tube 2 → 212.5 ng/µL, final volume 8 µL
Tube 4: 4 µL TE + 6 µL from Tube 3 → 37.5 ng/µL, final volume 10 µL
Tube 5: 6 µL TE + 4 µL from Tube 4 → 35.0 ng/µL, final volume 9 µL
Tube 6: 8 µL TE + 2 µL from Tube 5 → 32.5 ng/µL, final volume 10 µL
Tube 7: 4 µL TE + 1 µL from Tube 6 → 51.0 ng/µL, final volume 5 µL
Tube 8: 10 µL TE only → 0 ng/µL, final volume 10 µL

steps.title: Dispense samples and standards
steps.instruction: Using a P200 multichannel pipette, add 2 µL of each sample to the center of individual wells of a Costar black microplate (catalog #3915). Load 2 µL from each standard tube into a single column of wells (A1–H1). Work quickly to avoid sample dehydration and seal or cover the plate after completing the column.

steps.title: Add PicoGreen to wells
steps.instruction: Pour the PicoGreen working solution into a reservoir, then dispense 48 µL of this solution into every well (including standards). Cover the plate with an aluminum‑foil‑covered Rainin lid and also cover the reservoir with foil. Gently tip the plate and tap its sides against the bench until the liquid fully covers the bottom of each well (minimum recommended volume 75 µL).

steps.title: Incubate protected from light
steps.instruction: Incubate the foil‑covered plate for 2–5 minutes while keeping the foil on to protect the reaction from light.

steps.title: Read fluorescence on plate reader
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a fluorescence plate reader and read all wells using the following settings: 96‑well layout, excitation 485 nm, emission 530 nm, read from top, endpoint mode, gain (sensitivity) set to 50. Follow any additional specifications of the specific reader.

steps.title: Analyze data and plot standard curve
steps.instruction: In Excel, plot DNA concentration (ng/µL) on the x‑axis versus fluorescence intensity on the y‑axis for the standards. Add a linear trendline, display the equation (y = mx + b) and R² value. Use the equation to solve for x (sample concentration) from each sample’s fluorescence reading.
